mission.name: XRP intelligence and prediction-engine mastery
mission.foundation: Barrot V3 execution, orchestration, safety and verification

source_capture_policy.admission_rule: Do not admit market or event features until original source bytes are captured, SHA-256 receipts are independently verified, event/publication/data-as-of times are reconciled, and source independence and point-in-time availability pass validation.

limitations: The Federal Reserve and OCC declined comment; reported outreach is not confirmed by a regulator statement.
Reuters attributes outreach to several sources familiar with the matter; identities and the complete bank universe are not public.
One contacted-bank source reported no service disruption and few customer inquiries; this cannot be generalized to all banks.
The report concerns bank cybersecurity checks, not an XRP-specific regulatory action.
The approximately 6.340 billion dollar figure is described by Binance as digital assets affected; it is not a disclosed net unrecovered loss.
The approximately 2.850 billion dollar frozen/intercepted figure is subject to reconciliation and market-price volatility.
The 98 percent affected-token-asset restoration figure is Binance-reported as of October 31; it is not proof that 98 percent of stolen assets were recovered from the attacker.
The statement that Binance set aside more than 100 percent of required funds is an issuer claim, not an independently audited recovery receipt in this artifact.
Binance says it was unaware of discussions between US bankers and regulators; this does not independently disprove Reuters reporting.
The rendered response did not expose an HTTP Date header or exchange event timestamp.
This is one venue and top-of-book only; it is not consolidated executable liquidity or a sequence-verified multi-level depth snapshot.
Last trade and current best bid/ask are separate observations; the last trade can be outside the current displayed quote.
Original response bytes were not retained, so no raw SHA-256 receipt is claimed.

event_timeline.description: Binance reports that five hot wallets transferred approximately 233.46 million XRP to an attacker-controlled address between 20:05 and 20:09 UTC, alongside assets on other networks.
Reuters reports that Federal Reserve and OCC supervisors began contacting banks on Monday morning, asking about unusual activity or service disruptions after the Binance incident.

Reuters publishes its report; the Federal Reserve and OCC declined comment, Binance said it was unaware of the bank-regulator discussions, and one contacted-bank source reported no service disruption.

claims.claim: Reuters reports that Federal Reserve and OCC supervisors contacted banks on November 2 about unusual activity or service disruptions following the Binance incident.
limitations: Both agencies declined comment.
The contacted-bank universe is not disclosed.
No formal enforcement action, rulemaking, public supervisory order or XRP-specific action is established.

claims.claim: One source at a contacted bank told Reuters that its services had not been disrupted and customers had made few inquiries.
limitations: One bank source cannot establish that every contacted institution experienced no disruption.
No independent bank statement was identified.

claims.claim: Binance said it was unaware of discussions between bankers and regulators and whether the incident affected US banks.
limitations: This is Binance stated awareness, not a denial that supervisory outreach occurred.

claims.claim: Binance described approximately 6.340 billion dollars in digital assets as affected by the incident.
limitations: Do not relabel the gross affected value as net loss, net unrecovered value, customer loss or XRP exposure.
No independently reconciled net unrecovered amount is supplied here.

claims.claim: Binance reported approximately 2.850 billion dollars in digital assets frozen or intercepted, subject to reconciliation and market-price volatility.
Binance said 98 percent of affected token assets had been restored as of October 31 and it was acquiring the remaining less-liquid assets.
limitations: Replenishment by Binance is not the same as recovery of stolen assets from the attacker.
The percentage denominator and token-level reconciliation are not independently reproduced here.

spot.interpretation: Single-venue ticker and top-of-book observation. Do not infer consolidated depth, institutional demand or causal price impact from the Binance incident.

competing_hypotheses.statement: The reported supervisory outreach reflects precautionary bank operational-risk checks after a high-value exchange security incident.
disconfirming_or_limiting_evidence: One contacted-bank source reported no service disruption and few customer inquiries.

competing_hypotheses.statement: The outreach, if accurately reported, may have been narrow and informational rather than evidence of broad financial-system contagion.
disconfirming_or_limiting_evidence: The full bank universe and supervisory questions are not public.

competing_hypotheses.statement: The 6.34 billion dollar figure is a gross affected-asset measure, not the net unrecovered loss or a measure of XRP-specific loss.
disconfirming_or_limiting_evidence: The complete token-by-token reconciliation and independent audit are not included in the public post reviewed here.

competing_hypotheses.statement: The Binance incident may create temporary exchange-counterparty and custody-risk reassessment without producing a measurable XRP spot-flow effect.
disconfirming_or_limiting_evidence: No causal event study, synchronized exchange flows or XRP-specific institutional exposure change is available.

predictions.reason: The market observation lacks raw bytes, independent time anchoring and synchronized cross-venue context; the supervisory-outreach report is not an official regulator confirmation and supplies no XRP-specific causal feature.

next_tests: Seek a primary Federal Reserve or OCC statement, or additional independently sourced reporting, before upgrading the supervisory-outreach claim.
Reconcile Binance gross affected value, frozen/intercepted amount and replenishment against token-level Proof of Reserves and independent forensic reports; do not infer net loss by subtraction.
Continue tracking the 233.46 million XRP incident transfer separately from organic exchange flows; require ledger transaction hashes and recipient/exchange attribution before classifying any sale.
Capture original Kraken and Binance API response bytes with SHA-256, HTTP Date headers and exchange event timestamps before feature admission.
Run a timestamped event study only after synchronized market, depth, derivatives and flow data are available; compare with non-event control windows and preserve the no-effect hypothesis.
